subject: Data retention and PII handling - follow up from demo
messages:
From: Jessica Turner <jessica.turner@acme.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ben Lo <ben.lo@acme.com>
Date: Mon, 10 Aug 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Data retention and PII handling - follow up from demo
Attachments: acme-data-retention-requirements.pdf

Hi Camila,

Thanks again for the demo this morning - Ben and I appreciated the quick overview of Redwood's routing and caching model. A couple of follow-ups from our security/privacy team so we can move to procurement:

- Our primary ask is a 0-retention option for any PII that touches the inference request/response pipeline (names, emails, payment identifiers). We need assurance that those payloads are not stored beyond ephemeral processing.
- For non-PII telemetry/logging (health/metrics), we can accept shortened retention (30 days), but we need a scrubbed log option so traces don't contain user prompts.
- Any data residency guarantees? We prefer US-only storage for this project.
- Please share any SOC 2 / KMS / key management notes and a mapping of what logs are kept at which layer.

I attached our internal retention/PII policy for reference. Can we get a short note on feasibility and an estimated timeline (and any cost delta for dedicated/private deployment)?

Best,
Jessica
Head of Integrations — ACME Corporation

From: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.ai>
To: Jessica Turner <jessica.turner@acme.com>
Cc: Ben Lo <ben.lo@acme.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 10 Aug 2026 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Data retention and PII handling - follow up from demo
Attachments: redwood-mapping-sheet.xlsx

Hi Jessica / Ben — thanks for the clear notes and the attachment. Short answers up front: we can support your requirements, but the implementation path and timeline depends on whether you use hosted Redwood API vs Dedicated/Private deployment.

Summary of feasible options:
- Hosted API: default telemetry/metrics logs retained (30d by default) with redaction tools. We can perform prompt redaction and PII masking before logs are persisted, but we cannot offer a platform-level 0-retention guarantee for hosted multi-tenant unless you opt into a Dedicated/Private deployment.
- Dedicated capacity / Private (VPC/on-prem): we can implement a 0-retention configuration for PII by disabling persistent request/response logging and using in-memory-only processing; requires contract-level retention exception and security/legal sign-off.

Next steps I propose:
1) Quick scoping call with our Security & Engineering (30 min) to confirm exact data flows and sample events (e.g., do prompts include payment tokens or just names?).
2) Marissa to review your attached policy and propose a contract addendum and the technical controls required.
3) Draft mutual action plan (MAP) with milestones and a timeline + ballpark cost delta for dedicated capacity.

I've attached a mapping sheet that outlines the log layers (inference runtime, scheduler, control-plane audit logs) and what we can redact/disable. Can you confirm the primary PII types and whether you need US-only residency? Also, is procurement likely to sign a 6–12 month committed capacity contract?

If that works I'll schedule the security call for tomorrow or Wednesday.

Thanks —
Camila Reyes
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.ai>, Jessica Turner <jessica.turner@acme.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 11 Aug 2026 10:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Data retention and PII handling - follow up from demo

On Mon, Aug 10, 2026 at 11:02 AM Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.ai> wrote:
> I've attached a mapping sheet that outlines the log layers (inference runtime, scheduler, control-plane audit logs) and what we can redact/disable.

Hi all — looping in security/controls. Short summary from our side:

- SOC 2: Redwood is SOC 2 Type II compliant; we have control descriptions that map to logging, encryption, and access controls. We can provide an SOC 2 report (redacted) and a KMS architecture diagram.
- PII handling: For Dedicated/Private we can implement 0-retention for request/response payloads by disabling persistent logging and enabling in-line redaction. For Hosted customers we offer prompt redaction and configurable retention windows (default 30 days, can be shortened to 7 days for operational logs), but we cannot offer 0-retention at the platform level without isolation.
- Controls we can offer: request payload redaction, field-level masking, transient KV cache policies (evict after session end), and contractual clause for retention exception.

What we need from ACME to scope the change:
1) A sample of the event payloads (anonymized) or a list of fields considered PII.
2) Confirmation of which logs (runtime traces, scheduler logs, metrics) you can tolerate being shortened vs fully disabled.
3) Residency: confirm US-only requirement and whether backups must also remain in-region.

Operational impact: engineering estimates ~2–4 weeks to implement a private PoC with 0-retention for payloads (depending on backlog), and legal will need ~1–2 weeks for contract addendum review. There may be a cost delta for Dedicated capacity — I'll work with finance to produce a ballpark number after we confirm scale.

I'm happy to run the security call and capture technical requirements. Camila — if you share a preferred time I'll join.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole | Security & Compliance, Redwood Inference

From: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.ai>
To: Jessica Turner <jessica.turner@acme.com>, Ben Lo <ben.lo@acme.com>

Subject: Proposed MAP and timeline - 0-retention PoC for ACME

Hi Jessica / Ben — per our thread and Marissa's notes, I've put together a proposed mutual action plan:

MAP (high level):
- Week 0: Security scoping call (this week) — capture PII fields and acceptable log types.
- Week 1: Legal review of retention exception language and sign-off on contract addendum.
- Weeks 2–4: Dedicated/private PoC deployment with 0-retention configuration for payloads, in-region (US) only.
- Week 4: Validation run and exec review; sign-off to move to production.

Deliverables: PoC deployment, SOC 2 report + KMS diagram, redaction config and instructions, contract addendum draft.

Open items for ACME:
- Confirm PII fields (please send an anonymized sample or a field list).
- Confirm willingness to commit to dedicated capacity (estimate required: expected QPS/throughput).
- Procurement point of contact for contract talks.

I can schedule the security scoping call tomorrow at 10 AM PT if that works — Marissa and Rishi will join. If you prefer afternoon, say the time and we'll adjust.

Link to MAP & docs: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1Retention-SLA-Draft

Thanks — please reply with go/no-go on the MAP and any missing items.

Camila Reyes
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Camila — thanks, that timeline looks reasonable. Quick Qs from procurement / engineering:

- Can you provide a ballpark cost delta for Dedicated capacity (monthly committed) vs hosted? We need rough numbers to brief procurement.
- For the PoC, can you confirm which exact logs will be retained for 0-retention config (e.g., control-plane audit logs vs runtime traces)? We'd prefer absolutely no request/response persistence and only operational metrics (CPU/mem) for 30 days.

We'll get you the PII field list by EOD. Procurement contact is Michael Grant (michael.grant@acme.com).

Best —
Jessica
